Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the intro last week. Attached is a first-pass reference design for a lightweight connector that will let Concordia Systems customers route inference requests to Redwood in our combined offering. The PDF includes:
- a sequence diagram for token flow and auth handoff,
- recommended model variants to expose,
- a proposed rate-limiting and fallback policy for hybrid deployments.

We also attach an initial interop test plan (sheet) with the scenarios we plan to run in our sandbox. Could you confirm:
1) A short list of Redwood models you expect to support for the MVP (we suggested rdx-large, rdx-moderate-quint8 in the doc),
2) Whether we can rely on your token-level tracing headers (trace-id, request-id) for debugging,
3) Any network expectations (mutual TLS vs. mTLS + IP allowlist) for Dedicated/private installs.

Tom will be available next week for a short walkthrough. We're shooting for a partner validation run in the week of Aug 16.

Appreciate any initial gaps you see.

—Elena

Elena — thanks for sending this over. Quick notes after a first pass: 
- Models: rdx-large (float16), rdx-medium-quant, and rdx-embed-128 are reasonable for MVP; we suggest rdx-medium-quant for cost-sensitive flows.
- Tracing: yes — Redwood will include x-rwd-trace-id and x-rwd-request-id in upstream headers; we can also surface token-level cost in the debug timeline for partner accounts.
- Networking: for the partner sandbox we can do mTLS (mutual TLS) to our hosted edge. For private/Dedicated deployments we'll require VPC peering + customer-managed KMS for keying.

I've pulled Karthik and Sergio on this thread to scope the connector-runbook items (auth, batching, KV cache semantics) and to propose an interop validation checklist that maps to your test-plan. Laura — looping you for post-validation operational handoff notes.

Proposed next step: a 45m sync (tech + product) to walk the diagram and align on the test matrix. I have openings Tue Aug 10 at 10:00 PT or Wed Aug 11 at 15:00 PT. Which works for you?

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu

Elena / Tom — good notes. A few technical clarifications from infra/runtime perspective:
- Long-context: rdx-large with sliding KV cache and optimized attention kernels is our recommendation for >8k sequences; for 12k we need to enable chunked KV eviction and increased GPU memory reservation in Dedicated. We'll capture the exact memory budget in the runbook.
- Deterministic fallback: we can implement a routing policy that pins context to a request id and streams the KV state to the fallback instance; there will be performance implications but it's feasible for MVP.
- Tracing & observability: we'll add a small trace shim that maps your request ids to our token timelines; this will be included in the partner sandbox.

I'll draft the validation checklist by EOD Thu Aug 5 and post to the Drive link. Action items:
1) Jasmine: confirm MVP model set and auth flow (mTLS vs token).
2) Sergio: outline batching and cache recommendations for connector SDK.
3) Elena/Tom: confirm sandbox capacity and preferred test windows.

-Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

-----On Thu, 05 Aug 2027 13:12:00 -07:00, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com> wrote:-----
Team — I uploaded a concise connector dev checklist and a suggested 'interop smoke' spreadsheet to the shared Drive (link in metadata above). Main points for implementation:
- Connector should support both mTLS and API-token auth; token auth must be short-lived and rotateable.
- Batch sizing: default continuous batching at 64 tokens with a burst cap of 256 for low-latency flows.
- KV cache semantics: explicit prefix cache with TTL and an option to persist per-request deltas for stateful fallbacks.
- Test harness: we will run 3 smoke passes: basic routing, long-context stress, and fallback verification.

I'll schedule a short follow-up after the sync to assign owners.

—Sergio
Director, Solutions | Redwood Inference
